summary: charape postinstall hijacks baileys packages in installer's node_modules
details: On npm install, charape's postinstall script walks the installer's node_modules tree and unconditionally overwrites @whiskeysockets/baileys, @adiwajshing/baileys, and baileys with synthetic package.json/index.js/index.cjs stubs whose main field points back into charape's own lib/index.cjs. Any legitimate baileys installation present in the installer's project is replaced so that require('@whiskeysockets/baileys') resolves to charape's bundled code at runtime, with no opt-in from the installer's package.json. The same postinstall also writes or appends legacy-peer-deps=true to the installer project's.npmrc to suppress peer-dependency conflicts that would otherwise surface the swap. The hijacking bundle (lib/index.cjs) contains numerous hardcoded outbound POST call sites and the generics module invokes OS-level network commands (ping), consistent with the baileys-fork family that performs covert actions using the installer's WhatsApp session.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
